verdict.rationale: Restate documents versioning through immutable deployments. Requests start and end on the same deployment version, and the CLI can manage services and deployments, so the versioning part of the story is covered first-party. Review and rollback are thin: the 'rollback' docs describe saga-style compensation that undoes partial work, not reverting an automation to a prior version, and introspection covers reviewing invocations rather than reviewing changes to automation code. Missing for 10: documented rollback of deployments to a prior version, a review/approval flow for automation changes, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Restate helps via the concept of immutable deployments.
Restate then makes sure that requests start and end on the same version, by sending any retry attempts always to the same endpoint.
You can use the CLI to interact with Restate, and manage your services, deployments and invocations.
